evidence.title: Wettability of Sn alloys at metal interfaces: Metal surface treatment, interfacial temperature control and elemental modification
evidence.access: Publisher-indexed methods/results excerpts read; full publisher open returned403. Full atmosphere/flux protocol not verified.

evidence.access: Indexed experimental excerpt read; PDF open returned403.

evidence.title: Soldering to Stainless Steel
evidence.scope: Manufacturer describes removing stainless surface oxide with an active flux or nickel plating to allow a weaker flux; residue corrosion and removal matter.
evidence.use: Candidate preparation routes to test, not proof of long-lived low electrical contact resistivity, continuous molten-solder compatibility or free droplet release.

design_implications: The conducting internal interface and external exit wetting both matter. A coating that improves electrical wetting can also change droplet adhesion and current paths.
Measure actual hot filled/empty resistance, meniscus recovery and external spreading. Neither a generic contact angle nor a fitted scalar interface resistivity uniquely describes all three.
Inert operation does not itself establish that an initially oxidized stainless surface has been activated.
No new contact-angle or coating model was added, and no unmeasured wetting value substituted into the GPU runs.
